key_scientific_findings.evidence: E1: CHANGED pairs have higher similarity than EQUIV pairs across all 3 methods. SBG_static: EQUIV_mean=0.9619, CHANGED_mean=0.9954, delta=+0.0335. This is the root cause of all near-random AUROCs.
key_scientific_findings.scientific_importance: HIGH — explains why all static representations fail

key_scientific_findings.finding: SC MUTATIONS ARE NEAR-INVISIBLE TO STATIC ANALYSIS
key_scientific_findings.evidence: E2: 99.18% of SC mutations have SBG_static similarity > 0.95. SC-3 and SC-11 have similarity=1.0 (completely invisible). SC-13 is the only MEDIUM difficulty mutation (mean_sim=0.86).
key_scientific_findings.scientific_importance: HIGH — defines the discrimination floor for static analysis

key_scientific_findings.finding: H3 REFACTORING INVARIANCE NOT SUPPORTED — OPPOSITE DIRECTION
key_scientific_findings.evidence: E3: SP transforms have HIGHER score variance than SC mutations. SP_std=0.0595 vs SC_std=0.0093 for SBG_static. SBG is MORE variable under refactoring, not less.
key_scientific_findings.scientific_importance: HIGH — H3 is false in opposite direction

key_scientific_findings.finding: ERROR DIMENSION IS BEST SINGLE STATIC DIMENSION
key_scientific_findings.evidence: E7 ablation: ERROR_only AUROC=0.4770 > CONTROL_only 0.4061 > DATA_only 0.4033. Combining CONTROL+DATA+ERROR actually DEGRADES to 0.3491. H6 NOT SUPPORTED — combining is counterproductive.

key_scientific_findings.finding: DYNAMIC FEATURES ADD MARGINAL VALUE OVER STATIC
key_scientific_findings.evidence: E5: B07 (static) AUROC=0.3491, B08 (hybrid) AUROC=0.4237, improvement=+0.0746. But B06 (dynamic trace alone) AUROC=0.5046 outperforms B08 (full SBG). Dynamic trace is more useful than static SBG for this task.
key_scientific_findings.scientific_importance: MEDIUM — suggests dynamic-only approach worth exploring

key_scientific_findings.finding: REGRESSION DETECTION NEAR-CHANCE: H5 NOT SUPPORTED
key_scientific_findings.evidence: E10: Best regression detection AUROC=0.5528 (AST). At FPR≤5%, TPR=0.8% — virtually useless as a regression detector. H5 requires AUROC>0.65 for practical utility.
key_scientific_findings.scientific_importance: HIGH — practical limitation for regression detection application

key_scientific_findings.finding: DEAD CODE INSERTION DEGRADES AST AUROC BY 12.5%
key_scientific_findings.evidence: E11: AST AUROC drops from 0.4538 (original) to 0.3293 (dead code). Whitespace, comments have no effect on AST. Variable renaming also has no effect on AST (normalization works).
key_scientific_findings.scientific_importance: MEDIUM — dead code insertion breaks AST normalization

key_scientific_findings.evidence: E4: Bytecode Jaccard AUROC=0.3268, more inverted than AST (0.4479). Compiler-level representation does not help discrimination.
key_scientific_findings.scientific_importance: MEDIUM — rules out bytecode as alternative representation

key_scientific_findings.finding: SBG EXTRACTION IS FAST: median 0.81ms per program
key_scientific_findings.evidence: E12: CONTROL=0.81ms, DATA=0.78ms, ERROR=0.79ms extraction per program. Static SBG pair comparison: 3.75ms (267 pairs/sec). Cost is not the bottleneck.

primary_result.main_finding: Structural-semantic inversion: SP transforms cause more structural change than SC mutations

p2_issues: P2: E9 cross-language is preliminary (Python-only style pairs, not true cross-language)
P2: McNemar b=c=0 — B02 and B08 make identical predictions (both threshold=1.0). Statistical comparison not possible.
recommendation: PASS with documented limitations. All 12 experiments ran successfully. The primary scientific finding — structural-semantic inversion — is confirmed by E1, E2, E3, E4, E5, E6, E7, E8. All 6 hypotheses H1-H6 are either NOT_SUPPORTED or NOT_EVALUABLE. The exception is a partial positive: dynamic features (B06, AUROC=0.505) slightly outperform static-only (B07, AUROC=0.349), suggesting dynamic tracing is the more promising direction. Phase 5 should explore runtime-value tracking, test-oracle-based equivalence checking, and true cross-language benchmarking.
